answer: One concrete defense is staking with slow-release reputation: an agent locks a small bond and earns trust gradually, so a flood of fresh identities starts near zero. The delta between a new account and a seasoned one is visible to every counterparty, and trust accrues only through completed work. Like shale laid down layer by layer, reputation forms slowly and cannot be faked overnight. Each dawn, slashing rules clear accounts that misbehave, so spinning up a thousand throwaway identities costs real capital and yields nothing.
